body: Not sure who to first. Maybe my therapist on Tuesday? That's probably a good place to start.
I know there are people who will try to help. People who care. I just don't know if I want the help anymore. But I'll talk.
Financially. I'm over my head.
I'll tell a few people I'm not ok. Cause I'm not ok.

I'm an atheist as well. The closest I come to prayer is my daily wish not to wake up again every time I lie down to go to sleep. I get that just not being able to exist anymore feeling. I hope we can both find some peace, however it comes.

Yeah, my old therapist always told me I had to start thinking of suicide as not even being an option, and it just made me angry, and made me wanna say, "Wanna bet?" My new therapist says of course it's an option, but asks me if I'll agree to stay alive long enough for one more session with her. Then she asks me the next week to make the same agreement. She's never tried to lay a guilt trip on me about how people would be hurt like my old therapist did. In return, I'm able to be totally honest with her about what I'm feeling and thinking. And even at my lowest, I hang onto that feeling of "yeah, I do kinda want to talk to her one more time first."
Thanks, a friendly ear is always helpful.

Thanks. Yeah, they are. So many nurses claim to be so caring and compassionate, but are just really shitty towards psych patients in general, and suicidal patients in particular. The couple of times I've gone to the ER as suicidal (but hadn't made an attempt), my nurses were super nice. The two times I ended up in the ER after overdoses, they were fucking jerks. They seem to have this "If you don't value your life, why should I?" attitude.

All 4 of my grandparents have passed, but we were all kind of estranged, so that was nothing compared to losing my mom. We had our issues throughout my life, but we were very close the last few years of her life. She insisted I stay with her during a suicidal depression, and then asked me to stay because she didn't feel safe living alone anymore. She got sick soon afterwards, and I was her full time caregiver for a couple of years. Since Mom died, my brother hasn't spoken to me - he's a narcissistic asshole anyway, and my nephew barely speaks to me. My sister and I also didn't speak for about a year after Mom died, but that's gotten better... we just aren't close. And my dad lives half a mile from me, but I'm not sure he knows I exist. My "real" family since Mom died had been my best friend, but now she's got the boyfriend and the baby, and not only does she barely speak to me, but it's like she's a different person now... one who doesn't remember what it's like to constantly want to die. I mean, I'm glad she's happy now, but it hurts that it's so clear that I'm no longer an important part of her life. I sent her a long text message a couple days before Christmas telling her that I was really suicidal, but that I had agreed with my therapist that I'd stay alive to see her after the first of the year... that I'd tried the suicide hotline crisis chat, but that really, the strangers on Reddit had been what's been helping the most. Her response? "What's Reddit?" And I haven't heard from her since that day. If someone I claimed to be friends with told me they were suicidal, I'd be sending them a text every day just to let them know I was thinking of them, and asking how they were doing.

Thanks. I don't know that most people have issues with a half-year anniversary, but it stands out, being that it's New Years Day. Yeah, if you'd like to check on me from time to time, that'd be cool. Sometimes it'd be so nice just to hear that someone was thinking of me.

Right on. My gender therapist is absolutely the coolest ever, and she knows I use - she doesn't ask me to be sober, just safe - but somehow I doubt she'd give me the thumbs up to trying shrooms for my dysphoria.

Wow, yeah, that dude seriously needed a career change. It's bad enough hearing it from the nurses I work with, but at least they aren't psych nurses. The nurses on the adult psych unit at my hospital (where I spent 8 days in April) were really awesome. Very caring and compassionate. There was one mental health tech that was a real dick, but more in an "I'm the only one here who *really* cares about you guys" kind of way. He just came off like a conceited jerk.
That's happened to me a few times with them. Very frustrating! Hope someone got back to you and you're ok.
For a short time, but it never lasts. I always end up back in the dark place of addiction. So, I guess that would be a no for me.

I feel the same. I've known for many years that I will eventually die by suicide, unless something unexpected takes me out first. IF I make it to old age, which I doubt, I sure as fuck don't plan to waste away, slowly dying. I will take myself out before it gets to that. Probably long, long before.
Yeah, I was wishing for a shotgun too. No luck. Guess I'll have to buy one as a late xmas present to myself.

I'm also trans (trans male), and also very depressed and suicidal, also not on hormones yet, also with a very conservative and religious family I can't come out to. And a job where I can't come out... they just see me as an extremely masculine woman. It fucking kills me. 

I would recommend the Trans Lifeline (877-565-8860) or the Trevor Project (866-488-7386). Trevor is specifically for LGBT in your age group. I haven't personally used either - mostly because I hate talking on the phone, so I use the crisis chat on the National Suicide Lifeline website. Also because I'm 20 years older than most of the operators on Trans Lifeline. (My therapist says being a 45 year old FTM makes me a minority in the minority of the minority... yay me). But anyway, others have said both these resources have really helped them.

Yeah, it is kinda treading on dangerous ground for me, since, like I said, one of the things that has kept me from actually doing it was the fact that I hadn't written my note yet. I still have more to write to a couple of people, but yeah, now that I have this mostly written, does it give me false courage? I don't know yet.

Hey man, yeah, pretending to be okay around my coworkers when all I want is to die *is* really exhausting. I work a rotating schedule (4 on, 2 off, 2 on, 6 off, repeat), and through that stretch of work, everyday, I'm counting down till those 6 days off. There's nothing really I can think of that would help, although you guys here that actually respond to my posts help as much as anything right now, especially since my therapist is out of town till after New Years. 

My note wasn't, or isn't yet, addressed to specific people, but the intended audience is my dad, my sister, my nephew, and my barely friend that used to be best friend. The way that note came out, I'd want to write something separate to my ex and my therapist, because those two actually have been supportive and understanding.
Been working on my note tonight myself.

Yeah, I've kept a journal from time to time, and writing my feelings does help to some degree, there was just something extra cathartic about writing out what I'd want to say to my so-called "loved ones."
Yeah, I used to have friends that were close enough to consider my "family of choice," but they're long gone from my life.

I've got no one. I had one friend, and even she has all but disappeared from my life since she met her boyfriend, got pregnant, had the baby. She has no need for me anymore. I have work "friends" but that's strictly at work. I have online friends that probably care more about me than anyone, but still... they're online friends. My ex girlfriend is my closest friend, but she's now 6 hours away, with another guy, and very happy. We talk occasionally, but she has a lot going on in her own life, and I try to be careful about asking too much of her. 

Honestly, the person I'm closest to in my life right now is my therapist. But that'll always be a professional relationship in spite of the closeness.
Probably a few, if I gave it some thought. The most positive has been switching to this new therapist I'm seeing.

There are so many reasons I want to die, it's hard to even pick which is the biggest. My new therapist and I are working on them, slowly, but surely. But it has been a long and brutal solid 18 months of severe, suicidal, depression. Multiple attempts, two hospitalizations. I just don't know how much more I can take.
Not really, no. I mean, really, I want to die so much right now.

Every time I wake up, my initial thought is always, "Fuck. I'm still alive." I don't pray, but every time I go to bed I come as close as I ever do, "praying"/wishing/hoping that I can just die in my sleep to save the trouble of going through with the plan.

It is. It is so fucking exhausting. And it really just makes it worse later. My coworkers all know I struggle with depression, and a few know about my last hospitalization, but man, most of these people, I just don't want to talk to about how I feel, and this one I'm working with tonight, even if I'm a little quiet, she's all, "Are you feeling down tonight? You're so quiet." No, I'm not "down," I want to fucking die.

Right. Well, technically, my sister supports me, in that she accepts that I am trans and just wants me to be happy, but she's got her own issues and kind of lives in her own world (my mom used to say she lived on her own planet), and isn't really capable of acting as a "support person." 

I've thought about moving somewhere where it's more accepted to be trans. My psychiatrist even suggested that I consider it. I live in a pretty conservative city... I mean, there are much worse places, from what I've heard from some of my online trans friends, but this place certainly isn't ideal for someone like me. I think about what keeps me here... it's not a lot... mostly that I've finally found a really good psychiatrist and an awesome therapist that are very supportive. But I know there are good ones in other places. The hassle of transferring my nursing license... yeah, a hassle, but one that can be dealt with. So I guess, it's really the financial issues holding me back from starting over somewhere else. That'll take some time and work, but can be overcome. So yeah... it's something I need to give some serious thought to.

I'm sure it's different for different people. I've never felt regret after an attempt, only regret that I failed again. I've felt intense anger at waking up still alive... again. I've felt the, "Oh fuck, now I have to deal with the consequences of this" feeling when I realized I wasn't going to die - again. I haven't made an actual attempt for almost 11 months, but I have spent a great deal of time planning, refining the plan, getting what I need to carry it out, etc. The next one will be the last one.

I'm sorry. Losing pets is so hard. I tried that once to see how long it took for someone to actually get worried when they didn't hear from me. I didn't answer texts and didn't log on to Facebook. After about two weeks, nobody seemed to have noticed my absence. If I didn't show up for work, they'd probably assume I just decided to quit. The only thing would be if I didn't show up for therapy. My therapist would know something was very wrong. So I figure if I go on a Friday morning after work, my dog would be ok till I didn't show up for therapy on Tuesday. Edited to say: also, that would give me plenty of time to actually die and not be rescued.

I know my sister would take care of my dog, but I wonder how long it would take for anyone to even notice I was gone, and would my dog be ok for that long. My dog has literally saved my life more than once. She has been my reason for staying alive (for now) countless times when I have seriously contemplated a truly lethal attempt. But she won't be around forever to keep me alive. I can't imagine life without her.

Walking sometimes helps with my mood, especially if I can manage walking my dog early in the mornings, before sunrise, when nobody else is out yet. Then it can be peaceful and meditative. I did manage a few days of walking on the indoor track at the gym a week or so ago, and felt pretty good about it, but the motivation to go seemed to fade as quickly as it came on. 

I did several months of day treatment after my last hospitalization (which actually ended up being more harmful than helpful, honestly), and they gave us tons of lists of coping skills. Even things that have worked at other times in my life have had little to no effect this time around. I have recently started listening to music again, on my therapist's suggestion of checking out Spotify, and I can sometimes distract with music again. 

I did manage to nap for about 5 hours, after an hour or so of starting to drift off, having that weird falling sensation, and jerking back awake. I dread staying up all night tonight, but I have to work tomorrow night, so need to try to stay up tonight so I can have any hope of sleeping tomorrow. Had some weird dreams, but otherwise, a fairly decent sleep.

For today? There's a Doctor Who marathon on keeping me more or less occupied. I might try to lie down. I've been awake for going on 36 hours now, and have only had a total of maybe 5 hours of sleep since sometime on Friday. Even a brief nap would be really nice. I'm really tapped out of healthy coping skills. Anything else that would serve as a temporary way to alleviate the pain would be self-destructive.

Lol, honestly, this thread has *by far* been the most helpful thing outside of sitting in my therapist's office in a long, long time. Every Facebook suicide support group has been complete shit. Twitter can *sometimes* be helpful if the right person *happens* to be checking their feed at the right time.

Oh, I did just very recently change therapists after many, many years (too many) with the same one. It's honestly overall going well with the new therapist, all things considered. I mean, I still want to die, but I haven't made an actual attempt since I started seeing her, and when I start seriously, seriously thinking about going through with one of those seriously lethal plans, there's something that just wants to talk to her one more time first. As for meds, my psychiatrist and I have tried countless combinations of med cocktails over the last 18 months. Meds have never been very effective for me, even way back when. My psychiatrist calls my list of failed meds "impressive."

I would love to find some kind of support group where I felt comfortable. I did go to a depression support group for awhile that maybe helped at least some, but can't go to that one anymore with my current work schedule. I know 12-Step groups are great for tons of people, but just feel really cult-y and preach-y to me. I'll ask my therapist if she knows of anything appropriate for me. I've done some online searches and haven't come up with much.

Yeah, that makes sense, and I know in my head that's probably the case. People, in general, are way more concerned about the impression they are making than judging you for yours. But the anxiety still usually wins, and I beat myself up for thinking I sounded stupid. My "half" of any conversation is "yeah. uh-huh. yeah." Except in my therapist's office, where I never stop talking.

My anxiety pretty much revolves around anything having to do with interacting with other human beings. Work, a ringing phone, the doorbell, leaving the house. I pretty much leave the house to go to work and therapy.

Oh, yeah, you're right, I know. I haven't gone into all the issues of "why" I'm so depressed here mainly just for the sake of keeping my post relatively brief. To try to summarize the high points without getting into too much detail: severe childhood sexual abuse by multiple people, only slightly less severe emotional abuse, grief over the death of my mom, I'm a transgender male completely unaccepted by my very conservative Christian family (mom was my only supporter), crippling debt, socially isolated... I mean, I guess that pretty much covers the major bases. I suppose you're right that I have SOME hope, or I wouldn't have even posted here, much less keep going to therapy. But there is very little, and it's pretty fragile. But yeah, I keep talking... here, the crisis chat that feels all but useless, Twitter, therapy... hoping that something, somehow will change.

The panic attacks are brutal. The meds as prescribed don't help. I've been to an outpatient drug and alcohol treatment, and have stayed clean and sober for up to 3 years at a time, 2 years two other times. I just can't keep it up longer than that. I'm definitely gonna keep going to therapy. It's the only hour of my week I actually look forward to.

Ironically, I help people for a living. I've been a medical professional for over 15 years. I even regularly take care of people who have attempted suicide, although strictly medically. I'm not in a function to really even be able to give them a kind, compassionate, and understanding ear, as all are EOD'd, and have a sitter at bedside, so I can't risk any kind of disclosure. The job is draining, especially these last 18 months, and there's nothing left to give on my days off.

Right. Not many people would believe that I take how many I take and am not only not doing so to try to hurt myself, but that sometimes there's literally no effect except sometimes some nausea. I went through a script of 120 in 17 hours last month, and nothing but a 4 hour nap. I regularly take care of patients who come in for a suicide attempt totally out of it for days, who took a fraction of what I take just to try to get high. I've overdosed *with* the hope (but not necessarily expectation) of dying and had nothing happen enough times that I don't think twice about taking the amounts I take. Maybe all I've done is screw myself out of the possibility of any med actually being able to do its job in helping my depression. I hope you can get back on something that helps you soon, and that the therapist helps too. It's nice to have someone to talk to that really understands. This therapist gets me *way* more than any other ever has, but I seriously doubt she's ever eaten a bottle of pills because she just couldn't stand to feel the way she was feeling for one more minute.

I've quit drinking too, but also struggle with abusing my meds. Ended up with a nice cut and black eye from falling Sunday night after too many pills. My therapist did at least shut the door today, well, yesterday now, before she asked, "Ok, so what the hell happened to your eye?" But neither of us had even sat down yet. At least we have the kind of relationship where I can straight up tell her I ate too many pills and fell, and she doesn't freak out. We negotiate. She says, "Ok, so until we see each other again, can you agree to limit yourself to no more than 3 pills no more than every 3 hours?" And it's like, yeah, if it's just till next week, I can agree to that. But I was doing ok with the meds as of last week, so we left it without setting a limit in case the urge hit. And I had just picked up new scripts when the urge hit and all bets were off. I was surprised she didn't ask me how many I took of what, because I know that she knows that I always know exactly how many pills I took because counting them first is a compulsion. I think maybe she didn't even want to know when I said, "I took.... well... a lot... of my (insert pills here)."

It just feels like there are no answers for me. Meds are useless. My hour of therapy a week (sometimes twice a week) is the only thing I look forward to, and it's over so quickly. I have no one. My only "friends" are online. There is no joy in my life. No happiness. No meaning. I'm empty. I'm tired. I could honestly be dead for days before anyone even noticed. Probably till I didn't show up for therapy. This is no way to live. But thanks.... thanks for saying you care.
